obligation: G112 -- reduce dispatch count by real fusion, and what that can buy

isolated_dispatch_floor.reading: From 2 rows to 512 rows -- 256x the work -- the measured time moves 1.10x and stays near 17.3 us. The compute is invisible; the whole measurement is the cost of committing one command buffer and waiting on its timestamp.

what_this_floor_does_NOT_measure: It is NOT the in-command-buffer dispatch cost, which is what a fusion would remove. Production puts 964 dispatches in ONE buffer with no per-dispatch commit or wait. This probe measures the harness floor, and separating the in-buffer term needs instrumentation this runtime does not expose.

the_bound_that_IS_measurable.statement: G093 measured 702 ns of host encode per dispatch. Halving 964 dispatches saves 0.338 ms of host time = 1.1% of the token. That is the floor of what fusion buys; the GPU-side term could add more and is unmeasured.

a_prior_measurement_IS_RETROACTIVELY_QUA: G111's evidence records the retiled argmax at 0.0131 ms = 13.1 us. That is BELOW this 17.3 us isolated-dispatch floor, so the harness could not have resolved it -- the '25.9x' was measuring the floor, not the kernel. This is the missing explanation for why that win transferred 0 of 0.326 ms end to end: there was no 0.326 ms to transfer, because the 0.0131 ms endpoint was never a kernel time. ANY isolated kernel measurement in this campaign below ~17 us is measuring the harness.
